functional.title: Category selection
functional.body: At game start, the service snapshots the active roster in roster order and indexes players from 1 through N. It draws a random integer from 1 through N, inclusive; the player with the matching index becomes the anchor and chooses the first round’s category. The index remains stable for the match. After each round, the first correct solver chooses the next category. The game uses the earliest accepted correct submission to identify that player.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a new game with 2-25 players, when the game indexes the start roster from 1 through N and draws a random integer from 1 through N inclusive, then the player with that index becomes anchor; when that player chooses a category, the first round uses the chosen category and its background.
Given at least one player solves a round, when the round ends, then the earliest accepted correct solver can select the next category.

No response and no solver: A missing answer counts as unsolved and advances to the next hint. After Hint 3 deadline the round reveals and awards zero to remaining players. If nobody solves, choose the next category uniformly from the six configured categories.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a player remains unsolved after Hint 3, when the round ends, then the player earns 0 points and the game reveals the correct answer.

Given an unsolved player submits an answer for the current stage, when the server checks it against the target and approved accepted-answer list, then only a correct answer is accepted and scored once for that stage; an incorrect answer does not change score or expose guess text to other players; and the target answer remains unavailable to clients until round reveal.

No response and no solver: A missing answer counts as unsolved and advances to the next hint. After Hint 3 deadline the round reveals and awards zero to remaining players. If nobody solves, choose the next category uniformly from the six configured categories.

functional.title: Answer stages
functional.body: The first answer stage has no hint. Each unsolved player gets one submission per stage. Once all unsolved players submit, the game confirms stage results and reveals the next predefined hint only to those who remain unsolved. This repeats for up to three hints.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a player submits the correct answer during the no-hint stage, when the game accepts it, then the player earns 5 points and their round score locks.
Given a player solves after Hint 1, Hint 2, or Hint 3, when the game accepts the answer, then the player earns 3, 2, or 1 point respectively.
Given a player remains unsolved after Hint 3, when the round ends, then the player earns 0 points and the game reveals the correct answer.
Given multiple unsolved players, when all unsolved players submit for the current stage, then the game confirms stage results and shows the next hint only to players still unsolved.

Given an unsolved player submits an answer for the current stage, when the server checks it against the target and approved accepted-answer list, then only a correct answer is accepted and scored once for that stage; an incorrect answer does not change score or expose guess text to other players; and the target answer remains unavailable to clients until round reveal.
Match length and stage timer: Eight rounds. Each of the four answer stages has a 20-second deadline; a stage closes early when all unsolved players submit.

No response and no solver: A missing answer counts as unsolved and advances to the next hint. After Hint 3 deadline the round reveals and awards zero to remaining players. If nobody solves, choose the next category uniformly from the six configured categories.

Given an actor is not authorized to perform moderation or catalog activation, when they attempt to change moderation status or publish content, then the service rejects the action; every change to nomination count, moderation status, and eligibility is auditable; and content cannot be selected for play until it has passed moderation and is complete in the curated catalog.

Moderation workflow: Roles are Content Moderator and Senior Moderator. At threshold, content enters Pending Review. A moderator other than the proposer approves or rejects with a reason. The proposer may appeal once to a Senior Moderator. Approval alone does not make content playable; the complete curated record must pass validation.
Suggestion eligibility: Wins are lifetime wins on one stable profile. A profile may have one open category suggestion at a time; each contains one category and exactly three pairs.

functional.title: Predefined content
functional.body: Every playable word pair has a predefined category, prompt word, target answer, and three ordered hints. The game uses this content at runtime and does not generate prompts or hints dynamically.
functional.notes:
Original v2.6 document ID: FR-04; canonical MCP ID: FR-CURATEDPAIRS-004. Imported from docs/word_association_game_requirements.md v2.6, SHA256 e356a7bdce8fae59d3f9a9d48dd471c5c05ec724b5734ba9ed14bec1a754ebc2. Original document IDs are retained as source aliases; MCP requires canonical area-qualified IDs. Baseline Phase6 evidence is historical; subsequent administration regression and source identity are recorded separately. Hosted deployment/provider entitlement remains Phase7 work.

Initial content/identity/nomination/suggestion record contract preserved verbatim:
Each content record keeps the prompt, answer, hints, accepted alternatives, and category reference together so each round is deterministic.

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `pair_id` | Unique stable identifier for the word pair. |
| `category_id` | Relationship category identifier. |
| `prompt_word` | Word displayed to players at round start. |
| `target_answer` | Canonical paired answer, held by the server until reveal. |
| `accepted_answers` | Explicit alternative spellings or forms accepted as correct. |
| `hints` | Exactly three ordered, predefined hint strings. |
| `background_id` | Reference to the category’s predefined background asset. |

A player identity record stores the selected entry mode (OpenAI OIDC or guest), the profile reference, generated public alias, leaderboard opt-out, and selected icon. Authenticated profiles are associated with the validated OIDC subject; guest identity persists in the same browser/device until site data is cleared.

Nomination records include the normalized candidate word, nominating player, submission timestamp, moderation status, nomination count, and future-pool eligibility state. A nominated word does not replace the required fields in a playable word-pair record.

Category suggestion records include the submitting player, proposed relationship category, exactly three proposed word pairs, submission timestamp, win-unlock evidence, and review status. Each proposed pair must be completed with the fields above before it can be played. Former provisional MCP ID: FR-WP-004. Replaced at user request with a subject-identifying ID.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a category is enabled, when the content catalog is checked, then every playable pair has a prompt, target answer, three ordered hints, accepted-answer policy, and category background.

Content volume and reuse: Seed 10 complete pairs per category. Do not repeat a pair within a match until every playable pair in the selected category has been used; then reshuffle that category’s eligible pool.

functional.body: A match contains eight rounds. When the eighth round ends, the game displays final standings. If the highest score is tied, sum each player’s accepted solve durations and add 80 seconds for each unsolved round; the lowest total ranks first. Players still tied share the same rank.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the configured final round ends, when players have different total scores, then final standings rank them by total score.

Given two or more players tie for the highest score, when final standings are calculated, then total answer time is the sum of each round’s accepted solve duration, with 80 seconds charged for an unsolved round; the lower total ranks first, and an exact tie shares the same rank.
Match length and stage timer: Eight rounds. Each of the four answer stages has a 20-second deadline; a stage closes early when all unsolved players submit.
Total answer time and final tie: Sum server-measured solve durations; an unsolved round adds the 80-second maximum round duration. Sort tied scores by this total; exact remaining ties share rank.

functional.title: Lobby discovery and matching
functional.body: Players can browse discoverable open lobbies or use quick match to join an available lobby for this game. Any player in a room can share its room code or deep link to invite others; a deep link bypasses lobby browsing. Joining as a player requires an available slot under the configured capacity. An invited player who reaches a full room can choose observer mode. Before the game start countdown begins, if a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If player/observer membership or readiness has not changed for 30 seconds before countdown, all players are prompted once for that room version to mark ready; any such change resets the interval. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning. If they mark ready before it expires, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while the holdout remains unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the countdown begins. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins, and a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discoverability. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID. These joins use the same atomic capacity check.

Imported from docs/word_association_game_requirements.md v2.6, SHA256 e356a7bdce8fae59d3f9a9d48dd471c5c05ec724b5734ba9ed14bec1a754ebc2. Baseline Phase6 evidence is historical; subsequent administration regression and source identity are recorded separately. Hosted deployment/provider entitlement remains Phase7 work. Former provisional MCP ID: FR-WP-019. Replaced at user request with a subject-identifying ID.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a discoverable lobby is waiting and has fewer players than its configured capacity, when a player browses lobbies, then the lobby appears as joinable; hidden, full, or started lobbies do not appear as joinable.

Given at least one discoverable lobby has an available player slot, when a player uses quick match, then the service assigns them to the oldest eligible lobby, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID, without exceeding configured capacity. Given none is available, then the player is offered browsing or room creation.
Given a player is in a room, when they share its room code or deep link, then another player can use either invitation to reach the intended room, subject to an open slot.

Given a valid room deep link, when a player opens it, then the game bypasses lobby browsing and checks the room directly. If a slot is open, the player joins; if the room has no open player slot, the invitee is offered observer mode.

Given a room is full and the start countdown has not begun, when a player leaves and at least one observer is waiting, then the observer who entered observer mode earliest becomes the final player in the roster, existing players move up to close the vacancy while preserving their relative order, and any remaining observers stay observers.

Given every player in the room has marked ready, when the final ready state is received, then the game start countdown begins immediately and the player roster locks. If a player leaves after the countdown begins, then no observer or other player is promoted or substituted into that player’s place.

Given all but one player have marked ready, when the room enters the holdout state, then the unready player sees a five-second warning to mark ready. If they mark ready before it expires, the start countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while they remain unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the start countdown begins with the remaining roster locked. If the room has exactly two players, the holdout is not removed and the lobby continues waiting; the countdown does not begin until both are ready.

Given the game start countdown has not begun, when no player/observer membership or ready-state change occurs for 30 seconds, then the game prompts all players once for that room version to mark themselves ready; any membership or ready-state change resets the interval.

Lobby discovery and quick match: Rooms are undiscoverable by default; creator may opt in. Quick match selects the oldest discoverable waiting room with a free seat, then stable room ID. The same atomic capacity-checked join command handles the selection.

functional.title: Lobby
functional.body: The room view displays the room code, configured maximum capacity, available player slots, current players, and observers separately. A game cannot start with fewer than 2 players. Any player in the room can invite others by sharing its code or deep link. The room identifies the anchor player. Before the game start countdown begins, when a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If the lobby aggregate has no membership or readiness change for 30 seconds before the start countdown, all players are prompted once for that unchanged state version to mark themselves ready; any membership or readiness change resets the idle interval. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning to mark ready. If they mark ready before it expires, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires in a lobby of more than two players and the holdout remains unready, they are removed and the countdown begins with the remaining roster locked. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins; a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. The room creator has no special readiness or start authority; every player has the same lobby controls. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discovery. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room with a free seat and uses stable room ID to break ties. A 10-second countdown begins when all active players are ready. If a player leaves after countdown begins, nobody replaces them. If fewer than two original players remain when the countdown expires, the game is aborted and the room closes.

Given a room has reached its configured player capacity from 2 through 25, when another player attempts to join, then the game rejects the additional player without changing existing room state. This is true for any configured capacity, including 2, 8, and 25.
Given a player creates a room, when they set a maximum capacity from 2 through 25, then the room stores and displays that limit. Values below 2 or above 25 are rejected.
Given a player is in a room, when they share its room code or deep link, then another player can use either invitation to reach the intended room, subject to an open slot.

Given a valid room deep link, when a player opens it, then the game bypasses lobby browsing and checks the room directly. If a slot is open, the player joins; if the room has no open player slot, the invitee is offered observer mode.
Given an invited player follows an invitation to a full room, when they choose to observe, then they enter without consuming a player slot and are bound to the player who invited them.

Given a room is full and the start countdown has not begun, when a player leaves and at least one observer is waiting, then the observer who entered observer mode earliest becomes the final player in the roster, existing players move up to close the vacancy while preserving their relative order, and any remaining observers stay observers.

Given every player in the room has marked ready, when the final ready state is received, then the game start countdown begins immediately and the player roster locks. If a player leaves after the countdown begins, then no observer or other player is promoted or substituted into that player’s place.

Given all but one player have marked ready, when the room enters the holdout state, then the unready player sees a five-second warning to mark ready. If they mark ready before it expires, the start countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while they remain unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the start countdown begins with the remaining roster locked. If the room has exactly two players, the holdout is not removed and the lobby continues waiting; the countdown does not begin until both are ready.

Given the game start countdown has not begun, when no player/observer membership or ready-state change occurs for 30 seconds, then the game prompts all players once for that room version to mark themselves ready; any membership or ready-state change resets the interval.
Host authority and countdown: Creator has no special start/readiness privilege. All players have equivalent controls. All-ready starts a 10-second countdown and locks the roster.
Countdown departure below minimum: Never replace a player who leaves after lock. If fewer than two original players remain at countdown expiry, abort start and close the room.

Idle prompt and readiness races: The 30-second interval resets on player/observer membership or ready-state changes. Prompt once per unchanged aggregate version. Deadlines carry the expected version; stale jobs are no-ops.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Back returns to the previous authorized screen and dialog dismissal restores focus to its opener without submitting, changing readiness or leaving room membership.
Unsaved content/editor drafts survive ordinary same-profile in-tab navigation in memory only; reload, tab close, session/profile change and permission loss clear them.
Explicit Cancel/Discard abandons the draft and returns to the originating screen without changing the saved record; a canceled profile edit restores saved alias/icon.

Returning to a privileged screen revalidates authorization; back navigation cannot restore cleared private data or another profile's draft.

functional.title: Future answer nominations
functional.body: A player who correctly solves during the no-hint stage may nominate a word as a candidate answer for future games. The game records nominations by candidate word. A candidate becomes eligible for the future answer pool only after it has at least 10 nominations and passes moderation. Before it is playable, content editors must create a complete curated pair record with the required prompt, category, hints, accepted answers, and category background. Nominations do not affect current-round scoring or progression.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a player solves during the no-hint stage, when the round results are shown, then that player can submit a candidate answer nomination; players who solve after any hint cannot nominate from that round.

Given a candidate has fewer than 10 nominations or has not passed moderation, when the answer pool is checked, then it is not eligible for future games. Given it has at least 10 nominations and passes moderation, then it enters the future-eligible answer pool but is not playable until its full curated pair record exists.

Given an actor is not authorized to perform moderation or catalog activation, when they attempt to change moderation status or publish content, then the service rejects the action; every change to nomination count, moderation status, and eligibility is auditable; and content cannot be selected for play until it has passed moderation and is complete in the curated catalog.

Nomination counting: Count unique player profiles per normalized candidate. A profile may nominate a candidate once and submit at most one candidate per eligible no-hint solve. Moderation begins at 10 unique nominations.

Moderation workflow: Roles are Content Moderator and Senior Moderator. At threshold, content enters Pending Review. A moderator other than the proposer approves or rejects with a reason. The proposer may appeal once to a Senior Moderator. Approval alone does not make content playable; the complete curated record must pass validation.

functional.title: Full-room observer mode
functional.body: If an invited player attempts to join a room with no open player slot, the invitee may choose to observe the game in real time from the perspective of the player who invited them. Observer mode does not take a player slot, submit answers, make category choices, or earn points. The observer sees only the game information available to the followed player. Before the game start countdown begins, if a player leaves a full room, the observer who entered earliest is promoted to the final player position; the other players move up to close the vacancy. Remaining observers keep their observer status. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning to mark ready. If all players mark ready before expiry, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires in a room with more than two players while the holdout remains unready, they are removed and the countdown begins. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins. If a player leaves after countdown begins, no observer or other player replaces them; if fewer than two original players remain at expiry, the game start is aborted and the room closes.

technical.body: The service permits nomination submission only for a player who solved the current round before any hint. An eligible candidate cannot be played until a complete curated word-pair record exists.

Nomination counting: Count unique player profiles per normalized candidate. A profile may nominate a candidate once and submit at most one candidate per eligible no-hint solve. Moderation begins at 10 unique nominations.

Moderation workflow: Roles are Content Moderator and Senior Moderator. At threshold, content enters Pending Review. A moderator other than the proposer approves or rejects with a reason. The proposer may appeal once to a Senior Moderator. Approval alone does not make content playable; the complete curated record must pass validation.

technical.title: Observer perspective and permissions
technical.body: An observer session is read-only, limited to 25 observers per room, and is bound to the player who invited the observer. Signed links carry inviter context; a manual room-code observer selects an active inviter from the roster. Observer queue order is transactional, with stable profile ID as tie-break. The service streams the same player-authorized game view that the inviter’s client receives, including updates as the inviter’s view changes, while rejecting guesses, category choices, and other game-affecting commands from the observer. Observers do not count toward player capacity or scoring.

technical.title: Room code handling
technical.body: Room codes identify the intended active room and reject invalid or expired codes. Each room stores a configured capacity from 2 through 25. Room-code joins and deep-link joins use the same authoritative slot check as lobby browsing and quick match. When full, a valid invite permits the player to request observer mode instead of a player slot. Before countdown, promote the oldest observer into the last player position when a player leaves a full room; break equal observer-arrival times by stable profile ID. Use an eight-character Crockford Base32 code, valid while the room is active and expired on close; close empty rooms after 30 minutes and limit invalid-code attempts to 10 per minute per session.

Room code, reconnect, creator departure: Use an eight-character Crockford Base32 code. Codes remain valid while the room is active and expire on close; empty rooms close after 30 minutes. Invalid/expired codes return the same generic not-found response; limit code attempts to 10 per minute per session.

technical.title: Private live multiplayer delivery and autonomous progression
technical.body: Configure authenticated Realtime and an independent durable deadline/outbox worker. Game state must propagate end to end to players and bound observers without relying on periodic browser reads. Preserve authority, privacy, idempotency and owned temporary-runtime cleanup.
technical.notes: Confirmed user requirements: actual live gameplay, repeatable UI integration at2..25, design updates and independent hostile validation. Source: phone stale-roster report and corrections,27October2026. SDK token callback, coalescing, lifecycle, independent worker and owned cleanup are implemented. New presence-body defect independently reproduced in Chromium;2red React tests now pass, real heartbeat browser regression passes with unread negative control and production-only body drain.532unit/acceptance tests, lint and production build pass. Updated strict game is rerunning; full2..25 remains pending. Prior25-player round1 failure and measured shared-cluster WAL stalls are retained. Volatile TLS harness preserves fsync/synchronous_commit but proves neither power-loss durability nor public capacity. Faster waiting-room fallback and hosted Phase7 remain outside this extension.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Actual private WebSocket subscriptions deliver only event/aggregate/version metadata to authenticated per-profile audiences; anonymous, cross-profile subscriptions and client publication are denied.

Repeatable browser integration creates real guests and room membership, enters a code, readies players, plays eight UI rounds, and verifies remote category, solve, hints, scores, reveal, reactions and final standings through actual private notifications and authorized reads while periodic UI polling is suppressed.

An authenticated server worker advances countdown and hint deadlines with all browsers offline, drains bounded durable outbox batches, reports deadline and publication failures separately, and preserves failed events for retry. Foreground requests never wait for an active worker batch.

The temporary HTTPS gateway serves app and Realtime paths while rejecting tenant management paths; private credentials and internal ports remain private. Cleanup acts only on its captured lease generation and owned resource identities. A separate-broker harness must own a separate strict-TLS game database/outbox; partial startup or unconfirmed cleanup preserves recovery identities and blocks replacement.

Focus, visibility and online recovery trigger authorized reads; concurrent reads coalesce one follow-up, older responses cannot lose newer notifications, and unmount/account changes prevent obsolete subscriptions after deferred authentication. Connected game/social safety reads use15seconds and disconnected recovery uses1second; cadence changes preserve in-flight/coalesced reads and independent display clocks. Presence responses are fully consumed before clearing canonical retries and refreshing; a body-read failure retains the exact retry command.
Real UI integration proves token renewal beyond the original120-second expiry and actual WebSocket close/reconnect followed by another push-driven game transition.

Repeatable browser integration plays real eight-round games at every player count2 through25, with UI readiness/categories/every answer and identical final rankings, using a separately owned TLS game database and private Realtime outbox. At most two UI answers are submitted simultaneously; local results do not establish public-tunnel capacity. Cleanup is truthful and bounded.

technical.title: Category suggestion eligibility and review
technical.body: The service tracks game wins for each player and unlocks category-and-pair suggestions when the player reaches 10 wins. acceptanceCriteria.text: Simulate lost response, reconnect, expiry and stale commands; assert same-command canonical retry, unchanged committed state and authoritative recovery.

A disconnect must not corrupt accepted scores or duplicate a submission. Reconnecting players retain membership for a two-minute grace interval; after it expires the room applies the normal departure rules. Client retries reuse the original command ID.

Room code, reconnect, creator departure: Use an eight-character Crockford Base32 code. Codes remain valid while the room is active and expire on close; empty rooms close after 30 minutes. Reconnect retains membership for a two-minute grace interval. Creator departure grants no special authority; remaining players retain control. Invalid/expired codes return the same generic not-found response; limit code attempts to 10 per minute per session.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Enumerate hidden/full/started/waiting discoverable rooms and concurrent oldest-room selection; assert stable ID tie-breaking and no capacity overflow.

Deep links containing a valid room code route directly to that room without lobby browsing, then use the same authoritative open-slot check. acceptanceCriteria.text: Exercise eligible no-hint nominations, one-per-round/profile, normalized distinct votes at9/10, independent review, rejection, one appeal and complete-record activation.

The service permits nomination submission only for a player who solved the current round before any hint. It stores each nomination against a normalized candidate word and records its nominating player and timestamp. Candidate eligibility requires both at least 10 nominations and an approved moderation status. Moderation status, nomination count, and eligibility state must be auditable. An eligible candidate cannot be played until a complete curated word-pair record exists.

Nomination counting: Count unique player profiles per normalized candidate. A profile may nominate a candidate once and submit at most one candidate per eligible no-hint solve. Moderation begins at 10 unique nominations.

Moderation workflow: Roles are Content Moderator and Senior Moderator. At threshold, content enters Pending Review. A moderator other than the proposer approves or rejects with a reason. The proposer may appeal once to a Senior Moderator. Approval alone does not make content playable; the complete curated record must pass validation.

An observer session is read-only, limited to 25 observers per room, and is bound to the player who invited the observer. Signed links carry inviter context; a manual room-code observer selects an active inviter from the roster. Observer queue order is transactional, with stable profile ID as tie-break. The service streams the same player-authorized game view that the inviter’s client receives, including updates as the inviter’s view changes, while rejecting guesses, category choices, and other game-affecting commands from the observer. Observers do not count toward player capacity or scoring.

Observer behavior: Maximum 25 observers per room. Signed links bind the inviter. Manual room-code observers select an active player as inviter. Observer arrival order is assigned transactionally; ties use stable profile ID.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Test valid/invalid/expired eight-character codes,10-per-minute attempts, atomic final-slot admission, empty-room expiry and generic not-found privacy.

Room codes identify the intended active room and reject invalid or expired codes. Each room stores a configured capacity from 2 through 25. Room-code joins and deep-link joins use the same authoritative slot check as lobby browsing and quick match. When full, a valid invite permits the player to request observer mode instead of a player slot. Before countdown, promote the oldest observer into the last player position when a player leaves a full room; break equal observer-arrival times by stable profile ID. Use an eight-character Crockford Base32 code, valid while the room is active and expired on close; close empty rooms after 30 minutes and limit invalid-code attempts to 10 per minute per session.

Room code, reconnect, creator departure: Use an eight-character Crockford Base32 code. Codes remain valid while the room is active and expire on close; empty rooms close after 30 minutes. Reconnect retains membership for a two-minute grace interval. Creator departure grants no special authority; remaining players retain control. Invalid/expired codes return the same generic not-found response; limit code attempts to 10 per minute per session.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Actual private WebSocket subscriptions deliver only event/aggregate/version metadata to authenticated per-profile audiences; anonymous, cross-profile subscriptions and client publication are denied.

Repeatable browser integration creates real guests and room membership, enters a code, readies players, plays eight UI rounds, and verifies remote category, solve, hints, scores, reveal, reactions and final standings through actual private notifications and authorized reads while periodic UI polling is suppressed.

An authenticated server worker advances countdown and hint deadlines with all browsers offline, drains bounded durable outbox batches, reports deadline and publication failures separately, and preserves failed events for retry. Foreground requests never wait for an active worker batch.

The temporary HTTPS gateway serves app and Realtime paths while rejecting tenant management paths; private credentials and internal ports remain private. Cleanup acts only on its captured lease generation and owned resource identities. A separate-broker harness must own a separate strict-TLS game database/outbox; partial startup or unconfirmed cleanup preserves recovery identities and blocks replacement.

Focus, visibility and online recovery trigger authorized reads; concurrent reads coalesce one follow-up, older responses cannot lose newer notifications, and unmount/account changes prevent obsolete subscriptions after deferred authentication. Connected game/social safety reads use15seconds and disconnected recovery uses1second; cadence changes preserve in-flight/coalesced reads and independent display clocks. Presence responses are fully consumed before clearing canonical retries and refreshing; a body-read failure retains the exact retry command.
Real UI integration proves token renewal beyond the original120-second expiry and actual WebSocket close/reconnect followed by another push-driven game transition.

Repeatable browser integration plays real eight-round games at every player count2 through25, with UI readiness/categories/every answer and identical final rankings, using a separately owned TLS game database and private Realtime outbox. At most two UI answers are submitted simultaneously; local results do not establish public-tunnel capacity. Cleanup is truthful and bounded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Exercise lifetime wins at9/10, one open suggestion and exactly three pairs; reject unauthorized/incomplete activation and require independent review.

The service tracks game wins for each player and unlocks category-and-pair suggestions when the player reaches 10 wins. It stores the proposed category and its three proposed word pairs as one submission, tracks its review status, and prevents unapproved or incomplete content from entering the playable catalog. Win counts use a stable player profile and are cumulative for that profile’s lifetime.

Moderation workflow: Roles are Content Moderator and Senior Moderator. At threshold, content enters Pending Review. A moderator other than the proposer approves or rejects with a reason. The proposer may appeal once to a Senior Moderator. Approval alone does not make content playable; the complete curated record must pass validation.
Suggestion eligibility: Wins are lifetime wins on one stable profile. A profile may have one open category suggestion at a time; each contains one category and exactly three pairs.
